# Data Download {#sec-data-download}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(here)

here("R", ".setup.R") |> source()
```

::: {.callout-important}
This manual is still under development and may be subject to change.

This warning will be removed once the manual is finalized.
:::

To simplify the process of downloading WorldClim data, we developed the [`worldclim_download()`](https://danielvartan.github.io/orbis/reference/worldclim_download.html) function along with the [`orbis`](https://danielvartan.github.io/orbis/index.html) R package [@vartanian2026a]. This function takes the job of accessing the WorldClim website, scraping the data, and organizing it for you just the way `LogoClim` needs it.

Here is a parameter overview:

```r
worldclim_download(
  series,
  resolution = NULL,
  variable = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  ssp = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  dir = here::here("data")
)
```

The first thing you need to do is explore the [WorldClim](https://www.worldclim.org/) website to select the appropriate data for your needs. With this information, you simply specify the parameters for the [`worldclim_download()`](https://danielvartan.github.io/orbis/reference/worldclim_download.html) function.

::: {.callout-caution}
For small areas, increase the data resolution to minimize losses from the conversion process. We perform tests using 1% relative tolerance for areas with at least 1,000 cells. We recommend following this guideline and using areas with at least 1,000 cells. See the [Near-Equality Tests](#sec-sm-near-equality-tests) to learn more.
:::

For example, to download precipitation data from the [Historical Monthly Weather](https://www.worldclim.org/data/monthlywth.html) data series, between the years 2020 and 2024, at the 10-minute resolution, you could use the following code:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
# remotes::install_github("danielvartan/orbis")
library(orbis)
```

```r
files <- worldclim_download(
  series = "hmwd",
  resolution = "10m",
  variable = "prec",
  year = "2020-2024"
)
```

Refer to [`worldclim_download()`](https://danielvartan.github.io/orbis/reference/worldclim_download.html) documentation to learn more.

## File Structure

The function downloads and organizes files into a structure required by `LogoClim`, so it is essential to preserve this structure. The organization follows this hierarchy:

```text
data
├── historical-climate-data
├── historical-monthly-weather-data
├── future-climate-data
```

The structure above assumes that the data will be stored in a directory named `data`, but you can store it in any other directory as well. You will just need to configure the data path in the model settings accordingly.

The data files inside the folders also follows naming patterns that must be respected. Each series has its own naming convention:

- Historical Climate Data:

```test
    wc2.1  _  10m  _  tmin  _  1970-2000  -  01  .asc
    _____     ___     _____    _________    ____
      |        |        |          |          |
   Prefix  Resolution  Variable  Period     Month
```

- Historical Monthly Weather Data:

```test
    wc2.1  _  cruts4.09  _  10m  _  prec  _  1951  -  01  .asc
    ______    __________    ____    _____    _____    ___
      |            |         |          |        |     |
   Prefix   CRU-TS Version  Resolution  Variable Year  Month
```

- Future climate data:

```test
    wc2.1  _  10m  _  bioc  _  ACCESS-CM2  _  ssp126  _  2021-2040  _  01.  asc
    ______    ____    _____    __________     ______     ________      ___
      |       |        |           |            |           |           |
   Prefix  Resolution  Variable  Model         SSP        Period      Month
```

This naming pattern closely resembles the one used by [WorldClim](https://www.worldclim.org/), but there are slight differences that must be accounted for to ensure compatibility with `LogoClim`.

Note the separators. They can change from `_` to `-` depending on the data series and its specific requirements.
